outcome: maternal healthcare utilization (minimum recommended prenatal care checkups)
cohort: The study included 54,733 live births in City A (2015-2019) and 25,849 live births in City B (2018-2019) in Guangdong Province, China.
finding: Rural hukou status is associated with disparities in maternal healthcare, including lower probability of adequate prenatal care (in one city), lower likelihood of delivering in tertiary hospitals, increased Cesarean delivery rates, and lower medical costs in both Chinese cities.
mod_finding: Mothers with rural hukou status were more likely to have a Cesarean section compared to those with urban hukou in both cities.
cross-section timing: 2015-2019 for City A and 2018-2019 for City B
